toc.text: Report types: joining the quote-to-cash model

html:
A CPQ implementation that cannot measure itself is just a form builder. Analytics turns the quote-to-cash data model into decisions: where is ARR leaking, which discount approvals are helping, which renewals are at risk, and is recognized revenue on track. Salesforce delivers this through Reports & Dashboards for operational visibility and SOQL aggregations for programmatic analytics. This guide teaches you the report types that join the lifecycle together, the metrics that matter (ARR, discount leakage, pipeline, recognition), and how to build dashboards executives actually read.

Learning objectives

  • Identify the report types that join Quote, QuoteLineItem, Order, Contract, and Subscription data.
  • Define ARR, pipeline coverage, discount leakage, and recognition metrics concretely.
  • Build an ARR pipeline report with filters, groupings, and summary formulas.
  • Design a discount-leakage dashboard from Quote.Discount_Percent__c and QuoteLineItem margin fields.
  • Report on revenue recognition using Revenue_Schedule__c.
  • Surface renewal risk with Renewal_Opportunity__c and Account.Renewal_Risk__c.
  • Use SOQL aggregate queries for rollups that reports cannot calculate.
  • Turn report outputs into Role-aware dashboards shared with sales and finance.

Report types: joining the quote-to-cash model

Reports need a report type that joins objects. The report types you will live in:

Report typePrimary objectJoined objectsAnswers
Quotes with LinesQuoteQuoteLineItem, Order, ContractPipeline, discounts, margin
Opportunities with QuotesOpportunityQuoteWin rate, quote velocity, leakage
Orders with Quote DetailOrderQuote, QuoteLineItemFulfillment, ARR booked
Contracts with RenewalsContractOpportunity (Renewal), Renewal_Opportunity__cRenewal pipeline, uplift
Revenue SchedulesRevenue_Schedule__cAccount, Contract, OrderRecognition status by period
SubscriptionsSubscriptionAccount, Product2Active ARR by product, churn, MRR moves
Tip: If the join you need does not exist, create a custom report type in Setup. A one-way outer join (All Quotes with or without Lines) is usually all you need for leakage analysis.

Defining the metrics that matter

MetricFormulaWhere it lives
ARR (annual recurring revenue)Sum of recurring line values normalized to one yearQuote.Total_ARR__c, QuoteLineItem.ARR__c, Contract.ARR__c
Discount leakage(List_Unit_Price__c - Net_Unit_Price__c) / List_Unit_Price__cQuoteLineItem fields + Quote.Discount_Percent__c
Pipeline coverageRenewal ARR / TargetOpportunity.ARR__c, Contract.ARR__c
Recognition statusRecognized / (Amount - Recognized_Amount) remainderRevenue_Schedule__c
Renewal upliftUplift_Percent__c across renewalsContract.Uplift_Percent__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c

Get these formulas agreed with Finance before building dashboards; the report type only shapes the container.

ARR & pipeline reporting

Pipeline reporting answers: "how much recurring revenue is in flight, and what will it become?"

text
Steps of ARR:
  Open Quotes (Total_ARR__c)   -> pipeline stage funnel
  Approved Quotes              -> committed but unsigned
  Closed Won + Contract signed -> booked, Contract.ARR__c
  Contract executed            -> renewals enter Renewal_Opportunity__c

Build the report:

  1. Report type Quotes with Lines.
  2. Column Quote.Total_ARR__c, Quote.Discount_Percent__c, Opportunity.StageName.
  3. Group by Quote.CPQ_Quote_Status__c, then by Account.Current_ARR__c band.
  4. Add a row-level formula Expected ARR = Total_ARR__c x (1 - Discount_Percent__c / 100).
  5. Filter out draft quotes with CPQ_Quote_Status__c != Draft.
text
Row-level formula  : Expected_AR__c = Total_ARR__c * (1 - (Discount_Percent__c/100))
Summary formula    : Expected pipeline = SUM(Expected_AR__c)

Discount leakage dashboards

Discount leakage is money given away beyond plan. The leakage view combines the quote discount with the line-level discount:

soql
SELECT Quote.Total_ARR__c, Quote.Discount_Percent__c,
       QuoteLineItem.List_Unit_Price__c, QuoteLineItem.Net_Unit_Price__c,
       QuoteLineItem.Discount_Percent__c
FROM QuoteLineItem
WHERE Quote.Approval_Status__c IN ('Approved', 'Pending')
  AND Quote.Quote_Type__c != null

Sort leakage into bands so you can see "where is it worst" instead of "how bad overall":

Leakage bandDefinitionAction
HealthyDiscount_Percent__c <= 10%None
Watch10-20%Review approval path
High20-30%Approval_Log__c deep-dive
Critical> 30%CFO review; pricing rules likely broken

Cross-reference with Approval_Log__c: a quote that went through a manual Discount_Percent__c approval and still sits >30% is either a pricing rule miss or an approval gap.

Warning: Leakage must be measured against list, not against the previous quote. Comparing Net_Unit_Price__c between rounds hides rule-driven price erosion.

Revenue recognition reporting

Revenue_Schedule__c holds one row per recognition period: Amount__c, Recognized_Amount__c, Recognition_Date__c, Recognition_Method__c, Status__c, Period__c. This is the finance view of the platform.

Report patterns that finance trusts:

  • Recognition by Period: group by Period__c and Recognition_Method__c, sum Amount__c.
  • Deferred vs Recognized: chart Recognized_Amount__c vs (Amount__c - Recognized_Amount__c) per period.
  • Per-Customer recognition: group Revenue_Schedule__c by Account__c with running totals, filtered to Status__c = 'Recognized'.
  • ASC 606 / IFRS 15 view: break out by method (Straight-line, Usage-based) to show distinct performance-obligation treatments.
soql
SELECT Recognition_Method__c, Period__c,
       SUM(Amount__c) totalAmount,
       SUM(Recognized_Amount__c) recognized,
       SUM(Amount__c - Recognized_Amount__c) deferred
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
WHERE Status__c != 'Cancelled'
GROUP BY Recognition_Method__c, Period__c
ORDER BY Period__c

Renewal and risk reporting

Renewals are predictable revenue with a probability attached. Renewal_Opportunity__c captures each upcoming renewal with Renewal_Date__c, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c, and Status__c. Account.Renewal_Risk__c and Current_ARR__c enrich the account context.

  • Renewal book: upcoming Renewal_Opportunity__c rows grouped by month, with ARR__c and Uplift_Percent__c.
  • At-risk book: Renewal_Risk__c = 'High' and Status__c != 'Won', summed by rep territory.
  • Uplift trend: average Uplift_Percent__c per quarter for renewals won, versus the Contract.Uplift_Percent__c target.
soql
SELECT Account.Region__c,
       SUM(ARR__c) arrAtRisk,
       COUNT(Id) dealCount
FROM Renewal_Opportunity__c
WHERE Renewal_Date__c = THIS_QUARTER
  AND Status__c IN ('Open', 'Quoted')
  AND Account.Renewal_Risk__c = 'High'
GROUP BY Account.Region__c

Aggregate queries: analytics beyond reports

Reports handle grouping; Apex/System.query handles logic reports cannot express, like percentile bands, moving averages, or "top N products by leakage".

apex
/*
 * ARR velocity helper: recognized ARR this quarter, by method.
 */
public inherited sharing class RevenueAnalyticsService {

    public static Map<String, Decimal> recognizedByPeriod(Date endDate) {
        Map<String, Decimal> byPeriod = new Map<String, Decimal>();
        for (AggregateResult ar : [
            SELECT Recognition_Method__c method,
                   SUM(Recognized_Amount__c) recognized
            FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
            WHERE Status__c = 'Recognized'
              AND Recognition_Date__c <= :endDate
            GROUP BY Recognition_Method__c
        ]) {
            byPeriod.put((String) ar.get('method'), (Decimal) ar.get('recognized'));
        }
        return byPeriod;
    }
}
apex
// Top leakage products: worst lines first
SELECT Product2.Name name, SUM(QuoteLineItem.ARR__c) lost
FROM QuoteLineItem
WHERE List_Unit_Price__c > Net_Unit_Price__c
GROUP BY Product2.Name
HAVING SUM(QuoteLineItem.ARR__c) > 0
ORDER BY lost DESC
LIMIT 10

Designing dashboards people use

Dashboard discipline for revenue teams:

  • One metric per tile. A 20-chart dashboard gets ignored; a 6-tile board gets read on Monday.
  • Time-bound filters. Default to current quarter; let users switch quarters.
  • Red/amber/green thresholds on every gauge: leakage > 30% is red, pipeline coverage < 100% is amber, recognition drift > 5% is red.
  • Role-aware sharing. Sales sees pipeline + leakage; Finance sees recognition + deferrals; RevOps sees everything. Use folder + dashboard viewer permissions.
  • Drill-down from dashboard to report. Every chart points at its underlying report so questions can be answered in one click.

Suggested 6-tile RevOps board:

text
[ARR Pipeline: Open]      [Booking: Closed Won]     [Recognition vs Deferred]
[Discount Leakage by Band][At-Risk Renewal Book]    [Uplift Trend]

Hands-on walkthrough

This mirrors exercises 13.1 (Build an ARR Pipeline Report) and 13.2 (Design a Discount Leakage Dashboard).

  1. Insert a small demo set: 3 accounts, 5 quotes in different CPQ_Quote_Status__c states, 8 QuoteLineItem rows, 2 Renewal_Opportunity__c rows, 6 Revenue_Schedule__c rows (one per recognition period).
  2. Create a custom report type Quotes with Lines (one-way outer join to QuoteLineItem).
  3. Build ARR Pipeline report: columns Quote.Total_ARR__c and Quote.Discount_Percent__c, grouped by CPQ_Quote_Status__c, plus the Expected ARR row-level formula and SUM summary.
  4. Add a second report Leakage by Quote with the leakage formula (List_Unit_Price__c - Net_Unit_Price__c)/List_Unit_Price__c * 100, grouped into the four bands.
  5. Build Recognition by Period from Revenue_Schedule__c grouped by Period__c / Recognition_Method__c.
  6. Build Renewal Book from Renewal_Opportunity__c grouped by month, filtered to Status__c != 'Won'.
  7. Create the six-tile dashboard using these four reports plus two summary charts (leakage gauge, recognition ratio).
  8. Set dashboard filters for Account.Region__c and current quarter.
  9. Add a dynamic dashboard component for the leakage tile and set thresholds (Health, Watch, High, Critical).
  10. Validate: open each report, confirm grouping/filters exclude CPQ_Quote_Status__c = 'Draft', and confirm the dashboard matches the SOQL from RevenueAnalyticsService within one decimal place.
text
Leakage row formula
= (List_Unit_Price__c - Net_Unit_Price__c) / List_Unit_Price__c * 100

Expected ARR row formula
= Total_ARR__c * (1 - Discount_Percent__c / 100)

Common pitfalls

  • Choosing a report type that drops quote lines with no line records (inner join) and under-reporting leakage.
  • Measuring leakage against discounted previous prices instead of list price.
  • Forgetting CPQ_Quote_Status__c = 'Draft' filters, so draft quotes inflate pipeline.
  • Grouping on summary (rolled-up) fields incorrectly, producing double-counted ARR.
  • Building recognition reports from Quote totals instead of the Revenue_Schedule__c per-period rows.
  • Ignoring currency across price books, causing mixed-currency subtotals in dashboards.
  • Over-designing dashboards: 20 charts nobody opens beat by 6 charts Finance trusts.

Key takeaways

  • Report types are the join layer; create custom report types where the platform default is too narrow.
  • The four metric families are ARR pipeline, discount leakage, recognition, and renewal risk.
  • Use row-level and summary formulas for leakage, and Revenue_Schedule__c for true recognition views.
  • RevenueAnalyticsService-style SOQL aggregations complement (not replace) reports for logic Reports cannot express.
  • Dashboards earn attention: few tiles, thresholds, role-aware views, and drill-downs to the source report.
